correctness.rationale: An explicit missing-colour lemma proves an iff criterion for legal single-edge recolourings and describes frozen states. Two independently programmed complete enumerations use GP(5,2) edges and KG(5,2) disjointness edges, respectively. Both exhaust exactly 49,920 proper four-edge-colourings and 109,440 transitions, giving component sizes 1 (multiplicity 960) and 24,480 (multiplicity 2). The independent Kneser script checks the frozen 960-state orbit and the full action of 120 symbol and 24 colour permutations. All programs passed replay against the actual included scripts. Finite exhaustive enumeration applies only to this exactly specified graph.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the canonical smallest snark and four colors its minimum edge-colouring palette. The state graph has 960 trapped optimal solutions plus two distinct connected classes each containing 24,480 solutions: dropping isolated states alone does not restore reachability or a single irreducible Glauber class. The missing-colour lemma gives a structural criterion for local moves, while the alternating action of S5 and the trivial action of colour renamings on giant components display meaningful symmetry. This is a complete natural optimal-configuration classification, not a mere extension of the already known chromatic-polynomial value.
